Is a confusingly-similar trademark about to register?

Type your brand name. This page checks it against every US trademark published for opposition or registered in the last ~4 months using edit-distance + phonetic + rare-shared-word matching. It is the same open-source matcher we benchmark publicly: 36 of 36 real USPTO §2(d) confusable pairs caught, and 0 false positives on 20 unrelated names. The published table has 65 rows in three groups — 36 must-flag pairs (36/36 caught) + 9 borderline pairs where either outcome is acceptable (6/9 flagged, informational) + 20 negative controls (0/20 flagged) — and is regenerated on every refresh. Free, no login, runs entirely in your browser.

Nothing you type leaves your browser — the index is downloaded to you. Source: USPTO Trademark Official Gazette, a new issue every Tuesday.

A mark published for opposition can be opposed — or an extension of time to oppose requested — for 30 days from its Gazette date. Miss the window and your only remaining route is a cancellation proceeding after it registers, which is slower and costlier. A weekly check on the day the issue lands is the whole point of a watch.

How it works, refunds, contact

Try it free first. The free 30-day watch costs nothing and asks for no card: give one mark and an email, and you get the same private alert page and RSS feed for 30 days, updated after every Tuesday Gazette issue. It stops on its own after 30 days — the page stays online and shows you how to continue.

Buying. Pay $29 on Gumroad and enter the exact text of your mark. No account of any kind is needed: within one refresh cycle (≤24h) you get a private alert page with its own RSS feed — open alerts/, type your mark and the email you paid with, and your browser computes the unlisted address locally (the page shows only your mark and public USPTO records — never your name or email — because this site is served from a public repository). Every Tuesday issue is matched against your mark and any hits appear on that page (subscribe to its feed in any reader to be notified; quiet weeks are logged as "checked"). The checkout also has an optional GitHub username field: leave it blank unless you want the private GitHub repository as a second copy of the alerts (then you are invited within 24h and can click "Watch" for GitHub emails). We do not send email ourselves yet: to get hits in your inbox, paste your page's feed.xml address into a free RSS-to-email forwarder such as Blogtrottr ("as soon as possible" delivery) — about a minute, and it works the same day. If we add our own email sending later, existing buyers get it at no charge.

What is watched. Every word mark in the two Gazette sections that matter: applications published for opposition (~10,000/week) and registrations issued. Design-only marks (logos without words) are out of scope. Matching = edit distance + phonetic + variant forms + a rare-shared-word rule (a distinctive word both marks share that is uncommon across the ~200k-mark corpus, e.g. VEUVE, KODIAK — common words like PACIFIC or DENTAL never trigger it); the matcher and its 45-pair §2(d) benchmark are open source, so you can verify exactly what it will and will not catch.

Term. 12 months from purchase, one mark, no auto-renewal: your card is charged once, and when the year ends the watch simply stops — nothing is billed again. Two weeks before expiry you get a reminder alert with a link to buy another year if you want it. Several marks: buy once per mark (multi-mark bundles coming; ask).

Refunds. Full refund within 14 days of purchase, no questions — request it through Gumroad.

Contact. Open an issue on the repo (no account needed to read; a free GitHub account to post) or reply to your Gumroad receipt — both reach the operator directly.

Who runs this. TM Watch is published by APProjects — the Gumroad seller approj that sells the $29/yr watch; receipts and invoices come from Gumroad, and refunds are handled there (terms above). The pipeline is an automated job that fetches each Tuesday's Gazette, rebuilds this page and runs every paid watch; it is checked on every run. Contact: the Contact link on the Gumroad listing, a reply to your receipt, or a repo issue.

Not legal advice. A flag means "a human should look", not "this is infringement"; no flag does not mean your name is clear (design-only marks, common-law rights, pending applications not yet published, and registrations older than this window are out of scope of this index). Data: USPTO Trademark Official Gazette weekly XML (applications published for opposition + registrations issued), public domain. Matcher source, benchmark and methodology: github.com/APVentureEngine/trademark-watch.
